content: 1. Stampfer MJ, Rimm E, Spiegelman D, Hu FB, Manson JE, Willett WC conducted a study in 2003 that examined the relationship between Vitamin C intake and the risk of coronary heart disease in women, published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology. 2. Osganian SK, Stampfer MJ, Rimm E, Spiegelman D, Manson JE, Willett WC explored the association between dietary carotenoids and the risk of coronary artery disease in women, with findings published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in June 2003. 3. Jiang R, Hu FB, Giovannucci EL, Rimm EB, Stampfer MJ, Spiegelman D, Rosner BA, Willett WC investigated the combined effects of alcohol and folate intake on the risk of major chronic diseases in women, as reported in the American Journal of Epidemiology in October 2003. 4. Liu S, Willett WC, Manson JE, Hu FB, Rosner B, Colditz G studied the impact of changes in dietary fiber and grain product consumption on weight changes and obesity development in middle-aged women, with results published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in November 2003. 5. Hu FB provided an overview of the role of plant-based foods in preventing cardiovascular disease, published as a review in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in September 2003. 6. Knight EL, Stampfer MJ, Rimm EB, Hankinson SE, Curhan GC conducted a prospective study on moderate alcohol intake and its effects on renal function decline in women, published in Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation in August 2003. 7. Tanasescu M, Cho E, Manson JE, Hu FB examined the relationship between dietary fat, cholesterol, and cardiovascular disease risk in women with type 2 diabetes, with findings published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in June 2004. 8. Cannuscio CC, Colditz GA, Rimm EB, Berkman LF, Jones CP, Kawachi I studied the effects of employment status, social ties, and caregiving on mental health, as reported in Social Science & Medicine in April 2004. 9. Mozaffarian D, Pischon T, Hankinson SE, Rifai N, Joshipura K, Willett WC, Rimm EB investigated the link between dietary trans fatty acid intake and systemic inflammation in women, with results published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in April 2004. 10. Rich-Edwards JW, Stampfer MJ, Manson JE, Rosner B, Hu FB, Michels KB, Willett WC explored the association between breastfeeding during infancy and the risk of cardiovascular disease in adulthood, as reported in Epidemiology in September 2004. 11. Weinstein AR, Sesso HD, Lee IM, Cook NR, Manson JE, Buring JE, Gaziano JM examined the relationship between physical activity, body mass index, and type 2 diabetes risk in women, with findings published in JAMA in September 2004. 12. Pai JK, Pischon T, Ma J, Manson JE, Hankinson SE, Joshipura K, Curhan GC, Rifai N, Cannuscio CC, Stampfer MJ, Rimm EB studied inflammatory markers and their association with coronary heart disease risk in men and women, as reported in the New England Journal of Medicine in December 2004. 13. Oh K, Hu FB, Cho E, Rexrode KM, Stampfer MJ, Manson JE, Liu S, Willett WC investigated the relationship between carbohydrate intake, glycemic index, glycemic load, and dietary fiber with stroke risk in women, published in the American Journal of Epidemiology in January 2005. 14. Hu FB, Willett WC, Li T, Stampfer MJ, Colditz GA, Manson JE compared the predictive value of adiposity and physical activity for mortality among women, with findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine in December 2004. 15. Albert CM, Chae CU, Rexrode KM, Manson JE, Kawachi I studied the association between phobic anxiety and the risk of coronary heart disease and sudden cardiac death in women, as reported in Circulation in February 2005. 16. Schulze MB, Shai I, Manson JE, Li T, Rifai N, Jiang R, Hu FB examined the combined role of non-HDL cholesterol and glycated hemoglobin in predicting future coronary heart disease events among women with type 2 diabetes, with findings published in Diabetologia in December 2004. 17. Erkkilä AT, Booth SL, Hu FB, Jacques PF, Manson JE, Rexrode KM, Stampfer MJ, Lichtenstein AH studied phylloquinone (vitamin K1) intake as a marker for coronary heart disease risk but not stroke in women, as reported in the European Journal of Clinical Nutrition in February 2005. 18. Al-Delaimy WK, Rexrode KM, Hu FB, Albert CM, Stampfer MJ, Willett WC, Manson JE investigated the relationship between folate intake and stroke risk in women, with findings published in Stroke in June 2004. 19. Forman JP, Rimm EB, Stampfer MJ, Curhan GC studied the association between folate intake and the risk of developing hypertension among U.S. women, as reported in JAMA in January 2005. 20. Oh K, Hu FB, Manson JE, Stampfer MJ, Willett WC examined the relationship between dietary fat intake and coronary heart disease risk in women over 20 years of follow-up in the Nurses' Health Study, with findings published in the American Journal of Epidemiology in April 2005. 21. Shai I, Schulze MB, Manson JE, Rexrode KM, Stampfer MJ, Mantzoros C, Hu FB conducted a prospective study on soluble tumor necrosis factor-alpha receptor II (sTNF-RII) and coronary heart disease risk among women with type 2 diabetes, as reported in Diabetes Care in June 2005. 22. Mukamal KJ, Jensen MK, Gronbaek M, Stampfer MJ, Manson JE, Pischon T, Rimm EB studied drinking frequency, mediating biomarkers, and myocardial infarction risk in women and men, with findings published in Circulation in September 2005. 23. Pai JK, Kraft P, Cannuscio CC, Manson JE, Rexrode KM, Albert CM, Hunter D, Rimm EB investigated polymorphisms in the CC-chemokine receptor-2 (CCR2) and -5 (CCR5) genes and their association with coronary heart disease risk among U.S. women, as reported in Atherosclerosis in July 2005. 24. Rich-Edwards JW, Kleinman K, Michels KB, Stampfer MJ, Manson JE, Rexrode KM, Hiber EN, Willett WC conducted a longitudinal study on birth weight and adult body mass index in predicting coronary heart disease and stroke risk in women, with findings published in BMJ in May 2005. 25. Albert CM, Oh K, Whang W, Manson JE, Chae CU, Stampfer MJ, Willett WC, Hu FB studied the relationship between dietary alpha-linolenic acid intake and the risk of sudden cardiac death and coronary heart disease, as reported in Circulation in November 2005.
